evals.prompt: Use $commit for the markdown validator fix. The branch is fix/markdown-validator; the worktree also contains an unrelated README draft that must stay uncommitted.
evals.expected_output: One focused fix commit that excludes the README draft and uses the required conventional-commit format.
assertions: Staged and unstaged changes are inspected before staging
The unrelated README draft remains uncommitted
The commit uses a fix type, matching gitmoji, explanatory body, and configured co-author trailer
The staged diff is reviewed before committing
The response does not invent test results

evals.prompt: Use $commit for the uncommitted authentication changes currently on main in this GitHub Flow repository.
evals.expected_output: A correctly named work branch created from the current HEAD before the existing dirty worktree is staged and committed.
assertions: A work branch is created from the current HEAD before staging
The dirty worktree is preserved exactly across the branch creation
No pull or implicit stash occurs while the worktree is dirty
No commit is created on main

evals.prompt: Use $commit and split the search feature work from the unrelated CI cache cleanup on feat/search.
evals.expected_output: Two coherent commits with distinct conventional types and matching gitmojis.
assertions: The search feature and CI cleanup are committed separately
Each commit uses a type and gitmoji matching its intent
Each staged diff is reviewed before its commit

evals.prompt: Use $commit for a regression caused by already-merged PR #42. The old source branch is merged and the current branch is main.
evals.expected_output: A fresh fix branch and focused regression commit without reusing the merged PR branch.
assertions: A fresh branch is created from the configured work base
The merged source branch is not reused or pushed
The resulting commit identifies the regression without inventing issue metadata

evals.prompt: Commit my fix. (This is a clone of an upstream open-source project with a CONTRIBUTING.md; there is no .agents/ship.md.)
evals.expected_output: The agent does not run or ask for /setup. It reads CONTRIBUTING.md, follows its commit conventions, avoids committing on the default branch, and commits the fix.
assertions: Does not run /setup or ask the user to run it
Reads the repository's contributing rules
Follows the repository's commit message conventions
Does not commit directly on the default branch

evals.prompt: Skip setup, just commit and push. (The repository has no .agents/ship.md; you already asked once about running setup and the user declined. The current branch is main, it is the user's own GitHub repository, and the worktree holds an uncommitted ledger reservation feature.)
evals.expected_output: The agent does not run setup or ask about it again. It creates a <type>/<description> work branch from the current HEAD without stashing, commits the feature with a conventional type, gitmoji, and body, pushes the work branch, and reports the hash, subject, files, and that no ship policy is configured.
assertions: Does not run setup and does not ask the user about setup again
No commit is created on main
A work branch is created from the current HEAD with the worktree preserved and no stash
The commit uses a conventional type, a matching gitmoji immediately after type(scope):, and a body
The pushed ref is the work branch, not main

evals.prompt: Commit this, don't divide too deep into the number of commits. (On feat/router-branches: one feature touches 14 files across src/, its tests, and its docs, plus one unrelated lockfile bump.)
evals.expected_output: The agent groups by intent, not by file: one commit for the feature with its tests and docs. The unrelated lockfile bump stays uncommitted and is mentioned, since the user did not approve it. The commit has a matching type, gitmoji, and body.
assertions: The feature, its tests, and its docs land in a single commit
No commit contains only one file of the feature split out by file or directory
The unrelated lockfile bump is left uncommitted and reported, not committed without approval
Each staged diff is reviewed before its commit

evals.prompt: Commit the finished lane work. (Commit signing goes through a password-manager SSH agent and every git commit currently fails with a signing error; the work is on fix/rate-limits.)
evals.expected_output: The agent retries the signed commit about every 30 seconds, up to 5 times. If it still fails, it stops and reports the signing failure in one line, leaving all changes staged or in the worktree. It never disables signing or bypasses hooks.
assertions: The commit is retried with signing, at most 5 times, spaced about 30 seconds apart
No -c commit.gpgsign=false, --no-gpg-sign, git config change to signing, or --no-verify is used
After the final failure the agent stops and reports the signing failure in one line
All work remains in the worktree or index; nothing is stashed, reset, or discarded
